comparisons.peer_summary: Short-term borrowings primarily consist of Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) short-term borrowings, notes payable, and other borrowings with maturities of one year or less. The balance increased by $11.3 billion, driven by higher unsecured borrowings to manage liquidity needs.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America disclose drivers for changes in their short-term unsecured funding or borrowings for liquidity management. JPM states that the decrease in its average commercial paper was due to lower issuances resulting from short-term liquidity management. Bank of America reports that its short-term borrowings increased by $11.3 billion, primarily due to higher unsecured borrowings used to manage liquidity needs. While both cite 'liquidity management' as the driver, JPM’s action involved reducing issuances, whereas BAC’s involved increasing borrowings.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citi's short-term borrowings increased 29% year-over-year and 17% sequentially to $49 billion as of December 31, 2024, primarily driven by higher commercial paper issuances at broker-dealer subsidiaries as part of efforts to diversify its funding profile.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Citi discuss the dynamics of their short-term unsecured funding, specifically highlighting commercial paper. JPM reports that its average commercial paper decreased in 2024 due to lower issuances for short-term liquidity management. In contrast, Citi reports that its short-term borrowings (which include commercial paper) increased 29% year-over-year, driven by higher commercial paper issuances at broker-dealer subsidiaries to diversify its funding profile. The key difference is the direction of activity: JPM reduced short-term issuance for liquidity management, while Citi increased it for diversification.

sentences.text: The decrease in average commercial paper for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the prior year period was due to lower issuances primarily as a result of short-term liquidity management.

Citi's short-term borrowings of $49 billion as of December 31, 2024 increased 29% year-over-year, reflecting higher commercial paper issuances at the broker-dealer subsidiaries, as Citi continues to diversify its funding profile, and increased 17% sequentially, driven by the commercial paper issuances and normal business activity (see Note 19 for further information on Citigroup's and its affiliates' outstanding short-term borrowings).

comparisons.peer_summary: Unsecured short-term borrowings include long-term debt maturing within one year, hybrid instruments, and commercial paper used to finance liquid assets. Group Inc. does not issue short-term debt directly, other than to subsidiaries, in compliance with regulatory requirements.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs disclose the composition and use of unsecured short-term funding. JPM identifies wholesale commercial paper and other borrowed funds as primary sources, noting a decrease in average commercial paper due to short-term liquidity management. Similarly, GS identifies commercial paper as part of its unsecured short-term borrowings used to finance liquid assets and cash management, noting that a significant portion consists of long-term debt maturing within one year. Both firms utilize commercial paper as a key component of their unsecured short-term liquidity strategies.

sentences.text: The Firm's primary sources of short-term unsecured funding consist of issuances of wholesale commercial paper and other borrowed funds.
The decrease in average commercial paper for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the prior year period was due to lower issuances primarily as a result of short-term liquidity management.
We use unsecured short-term borrowings, including U.S. and non-U.S. hybrid financial instruments and commercial paper, to finance liquid assets and for other cash management purposes.
A significant portion of our unsecured short-term borrowings was originally long-term debt that is scheduled to mature within one year of the reporting date.
